text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert - Argus (tenant: argus-corp) on dedicated pool us-west-2. 99th percentile inference latency spiked >5s since 14:02 UTC. Error rate stable. Paging on-call: @jamie_oncall.

jamie_oncall: Saw the page, taking lead. Anyone on-call with Argus history?

samina_dev: I handled a similar tail-last-week. I'm available to co-run. Jamie, can you post perf graphs & tenant id?

jamie_oncall: Quick dump: tenant=argus-corp, pool=dedi-usw2-42, affected models=rwkv-13b-qat. Metrics: p50 ~80ms, p95 ~450ms, p99 ~5.6s. Token inflight per batch jumped around 90k at spikes.

liam_sre: Looks like head-of-line blocking. Batches are growing due to a handful of huge prompts + KV cache cold misses. Recommend immediate scheduler tweak: lower max_batch_tokens for argus-corp to limit batch accumulation. Also consider max_concurrent_batches cap.

marisol_eng: Agree. We have tenant-level overrides in admin. I can apply a temporary override to force smaller batches for argus-corp and isolate its queue to a dedicated worker shard if needed.

samina_dev: If we reduce max_batch_tokens too much we'll spike per-token cost; but it's acceptable short-term to stop tail latency. Suggest setting max_batch_tokens=2048 and max_concurrent_batches=6 then monitor.

jamie_oncall: Ready to apply. Marisol, can you run the change and share the command so I can ack with PD?

marisol_eng: Running now. Command I use (internal admin API):

```
curl -sS -X POST https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/tenants/argus-corp/overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scheduler":{"max_batch_tokens":2048,"max_concurrent_batches":6},"queue_shaper":{"isolate":true}}'
```

marisol_eng: Also set via control plane cli for audit: `rctl set tenant argus-corp scheduler.max_batch_tokens=2048 scheduler.max_concurrent_batches=6 --reason "live mitigation p99 spike"`

incident-bot: Change request received and queued for prod rollout.

marisol_eng: Applied override at 14:12 UTC. Reloaded scheduler on pool-dedi-usw2-42.

jamie_oncall: Observability note: watching p99 and tail distribution. Ops, pls post the next 5m snapshot.

liam_sre: Early numbers: 14:15 snapshot -> p99 down to ~1.3s, p95 ~320ms. Inflight batch token sum reduced ~72%. Throughput down ~12% vs baseline, error rate unchanged. :white_check_mark:

argus_ops: Confirming from customer side: call center noticed fewer timeouts on long prompts. Thanks for rapid response. We'll keep monitoring.

samina_dev: Good. Two cautions: 1) smaller batches increase model warm starts, watch GPU utilization. 2) quality/regression risk: some long-context prompt fragmentation might change response behavior.

marisol_eng: Noted. For now we also enabled `kv_cache_prefetch=true` for argus-corp to reduce cold misses; command:

```
rctl set tenant argus-corp runtime.kv_cache_prefetch=true --reason "reduce cold miss during burst"
```

jamie_oncall: Logging mitigation steps in the incident ticket. Assigning follow-up:
- short-term (owner: marisol_eng): keep overrides for 2 hours, collect perf & correctness diffs on sample prompt set.
- medium (owner: liam_sre): provision isolated worker shard for argus-corp to avoid tenant interference.
- long (owner: samina_dev): improve batching heuristics (size-aware flush, per-tenant burst window) and add regression eval suite for large prompts.

marisol_eng: Will also schedule a canary rollback plan in case we see regressions. Current plan: revert override gradually if throughput impact >20% or customer reports semantic regressions.

jamie_oncall: Notifying support & AMs: @argus_ops informed. Posting summary to #customer-impact with mitigation notes.

argus_ops: Appreciate the quick loop. We requested a follow-up RCA and any config implications for our future deployments.

liam_sre: For the RCA we'll collect: scheduler traces, batch composition histograms pre/post-change, KV cache hit metrics, and sample request/response pairs. Also will include the exact rctl + API commands used.

samina_dev: One more idea for medium-term: tenant-specific `max_batch_tokens` ramps based on 1min burst detection + graceful degrade to smaller tokens automatically. Adds complexity but reduces manual interventions.

jamie_oncall: Agreed. For now incident status -> mitigated. Keeping thread open for next-hour watch. If p99 creeps back up re-escalate. Thanks team. :bow:
